summary: The interpreter-level containment (PMA lookup, page walk restricted to RAM, TLB slot verification, device dispatch, shadow/uarch ranges outside the PMA list, fetch across page/PMA ends, CSR protection of mcycle/imcyclemax/iunrep/revert root hash) held up under code review and under ~1M differential native-vs-uarch random-instruction cycles (with and without Sv39 page tables, also under ASan/UBSan). No direct guest escape found. The candidates are guest-driven host-resource defects (R8 last bullet / R12) in support players and in the honest-operator claim builder.

candidates.title: PRT player keeps one hash per guest output for the whole input in the same pass that computes the claim (memory grows with the number of outputs), and logs one anomaly line per oversized output
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'); stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua: player_meta.__index:run_to_input_mcycle_offset (lines ~2066-2123: pending_output_hashes table, on_yield_automatic callback at ~2083-2091, report_anomaly('oversized_output') at ~2085-2087), run_to_stop (~1396-1409), flush_pending_outputs (~1419-1437); called with last_output={} from player_meta.__index:run_next_input (~2242-2270) for every input of the epoch run, i.e. the run that builds the mcycle computation hash (self.epoch_builder).
candidates.description: During the epoch run that computes the honest claim, every TX_OUTPUT automatic yield appends keccak(output) to the Lua table pending_output_hashes, which lives until the input reaches its fixed point (up to MAX_MCYCLES_PER_ADVANCE_STATE = 2^48 mcycles). Only at an accepted manual yield are the hashes folded into the 64-entry outputs frontier; on rejection they are discarded. So the player's memory during claim computation grows linearly with the number of outputs a single input emits (measured ~64 bytes of Lua heap per output; a guest can emit one output every 2 mcycles). The frontier could be updated incrementally on a copy (O(64) hashes) and the copy discarded on rejection, so the growth is not required by the semantics. In addition, each output whose declared length exceeds the tx buffer triggers report_anomaly('oversized_output'), which writes one stderr line (or calls the handler) per output, so log storage also grows with the number of outputs. Each output also costs the player a receive_cmio_request of up to 2 MiB over JSON-RPC plus a 2 MiB keccak (measured ~5 ms per yield locally, without RPC, vs 0.0035 us per plain mcycle).
candidates.trigger: Any input sender: the input takes control of the guest (section 4) and loops 'sd t1,0(t4); j .' with t4 = HTIF tohost and t1 = DEV yield, CMD automatic, REASON TX_OUTPUT, DATA = 0 (memory per output) or DATA = 2 MiB / > 2 MiB (time per output, anomaly line per output), never yielding manually until near imcyclemax.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from every valid template: R8/section 4 say any input may take over the guest and run any instruction stream; automatic yields are enabled in iyield in the rollup templates (the player itself handles them). Each output costs the guest 2 mcycles, far below the 2^48 per-input budget.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The exclusion 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields ... This holds as long as the memory and storage that the honest operator needs to defend its claims do not grow with the number of outputs, and each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12)' does not apply to the memory part: here the memory held while computing the claim grows with the number of outputs. 'Keeping outputs to prove them later is not on the honest operator's path' - but this player couples output retention to the claim-computing pass, so the growth stops the claim. The per-yield time part (bounded 2 MiB per yield) is covered by that exclusion under one reading.

2 Role: the PRT player is Support (AUDIT.md). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'.
3 High/Medium cases: as a support defect it falls under Medium ('A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium').

4 In the honest-operator role it would violate R12: 'The memory and storage the honest operator needs to defend its claims do not grow with the number of outputs' and R8: 'No guest action may ... cause unbounded host allocation', at a reachable state -> Critical in that role, hence Medium for Support.
candidates.threat_to_goal: If a validator used this player (or copied its design), one input could exhaust its memory while it computes the epoch claim (completeness failure: the honest claim is never posted or the player dies), letting a dishonest claim win by timeout. As shipped it is a support recipe, so the defect is a rule violation in the reference implementation of the operator.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R8/yieldcost.lua (local machine, same machine:run + receive_cmio_request + keccak sequence as on_yield_automatic): 200000 zero-length TX_OUTPUT yields in 399999 mcycles kept 12500 KiB of Lua heap in the pending table (~64 B/output); 500 yields with DATA=2 MiB took 2.53 s (5.05 ms per 2-mcycle yield) vs 0.0035 us per plain mcycle.
candidates.test_idea: Build a bare-metal guest (bugs/harness/baremetal) whose input handler emits K zero-length outputs via automatic TX_OUTPUT yields and then accepts. Drive prt.lua's player run_next_input on a local deployment (or call player:run_to_input_mcycle_offset with last_output={} and a frontier) while sampling collectgarbage('count') from inside on_yield_automatic (or hook report_anomaly); assert that the peak Lua heap during the input does not grow with K (e.g. heap(K=200000) - heap(K=1000) < 1 MiB) and that at most one oversized_output anomaly is reported per input. Fails today (heap grows ~64 B * K; one anomaly line per output).

candidates.title: vg.lua honest player retains every output payload (up to 2 MiB each) for the whole input/epoch and aborts on an outputs-root mismatch
candidates.role: Support (implementation of an operator that no deployment runs; documented in the manual's 'Verification game' section)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/vg.lua: player_methods:run_to_input_mcycle_offset (~435-480, pending_outputs[#pending_outputs+1] = output_data), flush_pending_outputs (~421-430: outputs[#outputs+1] = output_data, then assert(frontier root == outputs_merkle_root, 'outputs Merkle root mismatch')), event_handler:input_added (~563-577, passes self.outputs), event_handler:epoch_sealed (~583-602, keeps self.outputs and computes proofs for all).
candidates.description: On every TX_OUTPUT automatic yield the honest vg player stores the full output payload string (receive_cmio_request returns up to the tx buffer length, 2 MiB) in pending_outputs, and after an accepted input moves all of them into self.outputs, which is kept for the whole epoch. A guest that emits one 2 MiB output every 2 mcycles makes the player allocate ~1 GiB per ~1000 mcycles. Separately, when an input accepts with an outputs Merkle root that differs from the root of the outputs it emitted (an application that is not correctly designed, or a subverted guest), flush_pending_outputs raises 'outputs Merkle root mismatch' out of the input_added handler, so the honest player stops processing inputs instead of continuing to defend the state trajectory.
candidates.trigger: Any input sender taking control of the guest: emit many TX_OUTPUT automatic yields with DATA = 2 MiB (memory), or accept with a tx-buffer root that does not match the emitted outputs (abort).
candidates.reachability: Any assignment of guest memory/registers is reachable; a subverted guest can write any tx-buffer contents and yield with any reason.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Memory part: not excluded, since the memory the player holds while computing its claim grows with the number and size of outputs (the exclusion requires that it does not). Abort part: section 8 says 'An application that breaks the rollup interface may leave its outputs unprovable, but it must never stop the honest operator from computing claims or producing proofs. Development tools may instead stop and report the violation.' If vg.lua counts as a development tool, the abort part is out of scope; if it counts as an implementation of an operator, it is not. Facts deciding: whether vg.lua's honest role is meant as an operator implementation (the manual presents it as one) or as a development tool.

2 Role: Support. 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'.
3 Medium case: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium.'

4 In the honest-operator role: R12 ('memory and storage the honest operator needs to defend its claims do not grow with the number of outputs'), R8 ('No guest action may ... cause unbounded host allocation'), R4 ('This holds for every guest, whether or not its application is correctly designed') -> Critical there, Medium as Support.
candidates.threat_to_goal: An operator built on this documented recipe could be knocked out (OOM or Lua error) by a single input, eliminating the honest claim by timeout.
candidates.evidence: Code reading; the 2 MiB-per-2-mcycle output rate is the one measured by yieldcost.lua (see candidate 1).
candidates.test_idea: Use vg-test.lua's harness: run the honest player over an epoch whose guest (bare-metal) emits N outputs of 2 MiB then accepts; assert the player's Lua heap after the input is O(1) in N (or bounded by a few MiB), and a second test where the guest accepts with a wrong root asserting the player still answers the referee (no 'outputs Merkle root mismatch' error) and only reports the anomaly.

candidates.title: collect_mcycle_root_hashes returns at every automatic yield and its entry rehashes every page mapped by the write TLB, so a guest makes each 2-mcycle yield cost ~1 MiB of hashing
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md lists collect_mcycle_root_hashes and the hash tree as honest operator)
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp: machine::collect_mcycle_root_hashes (2424-2595: update_hash_tree() at 2451, loop break at 2558 on any break reason other than reached_target_mcycle, e.g. yielded_automatically); machine::update_hash_tree (1644-1648) -> mark_write_tlb_dirty_pages (1639-1643) -> mark_write_tlb_dirty_page (1619-1637), which marks the page of every valid write-TLB slot dirty on every call whether or not it changed; also result.hashes.reserve(clamp(...,1,16384)) per call (2481).
candidates.description: Each automatic yield ends a collect_mcycle_root_hashes call, so the caller must call it again for the rest of the period. On entry it calls update_hash_tree(), which marks dirty the page of each of the 256 write-TLB slots plus the always-dirty shadow pages and rehashes them, even though nothing was written since the previous update (the collect state access already tracks every write precisely in context.dirty_pages). A guest that first touches 256 distinct pages with stores (filling the write TLB) and then loops on an automatic yield makes every 2-mcycle yield cost a rehash of ~1 MiB plus tree propagation. Measured: 351 us per yield with a full write TLB vs 34.5 us with an empty one, vs ~0.13 us for machine:run to the same yield. Without the defect the worst case per mcycle of building a claim is about one page hash per mcycle (a new page written each mcycle); with it, ~128 page hashes per mcycle.
candidates.trigger: Any input sender taking control of the guest: store to 256 distinct pages, then loop 'sd t1,0(t4); j .' with t1 = automatic yield (any reason, e.g. progress) to HTIF tohost.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template (arbitrary guest instruction stream; automatic yields enabled in iyield). The write TLB has 256 slots indexed by vaddr page, any 256 consecutive pages fill it.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Two readings. (a) Section 8 excludes 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields ... as long as ... each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12)'; the per-yield cost here is bounded (256 pages), so under this reading it is out of scope. (b) The defect is not the number of yields but the avoidable size of the per-yield cost; the High case covers it.

3 High case: 'A defect that lets the guest, or host load that the deployment was sized for, multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect ... When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High'. The operation is 'a part of a claim' (R12). The rehash of unchanged pages is not required by the semantics ('A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect').

4 Not Critical unless the factor (~100x on the worst case, ~10^4-10^5x on a plain mcycle) exceeds what the deployment was sized for: 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make ... larger than what the deployment was sized for' would make it Critical. Facts deciding: the deployment's per-mcycle cost budget for claim building.
candidates.claimed_severity: High (or Out of scope under reading (a); Critical if beyond the deployment's sizing)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Slows the honest claim computation by a guest-chosen constant factor; if the clocks were sized on the cost of plain mcycles, the honest operator may not finish the epoch claim or its bisection re-runs within the dispute clocks (completeness).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R8/collectcost.lua (in-tree build, 4 MiB RAM, hand-assembled guest): fill_tlb=false per_yield_collect_us=34.5, fill_tlb=true per_yield_collect_us=351.4, per_yield_run_us=0.12-0.13.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test with the hand-assembled guest of collectcost.lua: measure the hash-tree work per collect call deterministically instead of time (e.g. via the hash-tree stats/counters API if exposed, or by counting pages rehashed with get_hash_tree_stats before/after), and assert that a collect call that resumes after an automatic yield with no intervening writes rehashes O(1) pages, independent of how many write-TLB slots are valid. Alternatively assert per-call time ratio full-TLB/empty-TLB < 2.

not_covered: VirtIO devices (unreproducible-only) and their host I/O (p9fs, net, console): containment of host files/sockets was not reviewed; R14 puts unreproducible nondeterminism out of scope, but host-memory safety of virtio-p9fs/net against a malicious guest was not checked.

WFI in unreproducible mode: poll_external_interrupts may set mcycle to mcycle_end and the loop then increments it once more (mcycle can pass mcycle_end/imcyclemax by one); noted but not developed because it needs an unreproducible machine.
Soft-float (soft-float.hpp) host UB was only exercised by the random fuzzer (OP-FP/MADD with FS on), not reviewed line by line.
log_step / record_step_state_access / replay_step_state_access (big-machine step logs, ZK-related) and the C++/Lua/JSON-RPC verify functions on guest-shaped states.
collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes and log_step_uarch per-call costs under guest-chosen states (only the mcycle collector was measured).
machine-guest-tools (libcmt, rollup tools) as the guest-side rollup interface; the solidity step and Dave contracts (other angles).
Linux-guest-driven tests (only bare-metal/random guests were used); the JSON-RPC server process behaviour under massive console output (host output channels are assumed to accept writes).
The differential fuzzer used random instruction streams with a fixed Sv39 table layout; it did not target sv48/sv57, MPRV corner cases systematically, or multi-page AMO/LR/SC sequences on devices.
